clue.text: Reassembled fleet with haste set out at night

indicators.note: something reassembled has its parts put together again in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A navy hurriedly regroups its fleet and sails off under cover of darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reassembled' rearranges FLEET and HASTE together. 'set out at night' sounds like ships leaving, but means put out on the bedside table at bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are typically removed and left in a glass overnight, so they are things put out at night.

clue.text: Guess when birds turned north

parts.note: 'as' can mean 'when', as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the word for birds runs backwards

parts.note: emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: Someone guesses the season from birds wheeling northwards on migration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned north' reverses EMUS to SUME, because a down answer read upwards runs back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to suppose something without proof, which is what a guess does.

clue.text: It takes a day to go round hunting on this

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: the day's abbreviation goes round the letter A, enclosing it

parts.note: Fri is the short form of Friday

explanation.surface: A riddle: what takes a whole day to get round, and you go hunting on it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as SA (sex appeal) is a crossword convention. FRI goes round A to give FARI.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition, traditionally in Africa, on which people hunt or watch big game.

clue.text: Sea duty organised for 24-hour period

definitions.note: a weekday is one particular twenty-four-hour stretch

indicators.note: to organise is to put into order, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A sailor's duty roster is organised around a full day's watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges SEA and DUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: This weekday is one specific day, and any day is a period of twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Your compiler sent up Irish leader in the East

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending up means reading upwards, so the pronoun runs backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so the word is 'me'

explanation.surface: The setter mocks an Irish politician who leads in the eastern regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses ME to EM; 'Your compiler' meaning ME is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a ruler or commander in Muslim countries of the Middle East.

clue.text: Old attend to layer that binds eastern ship

indicators.note: the bird's word binds, or encloses, the letters that follow

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs, so a layer
the ark is Noah's ship

explanation.surface: Instructions to tend to a binding layer on an old ship heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' means an egg-laying bird, not a stratum; 'that binds' means it encloses the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic verb meaning to listen or pay attention, so an old word for attend.

clue.text: President to rave about beer and go bananas

indicators.note: the word for rave goes about, enclosing, the rearranged letters

parts.note: to rave is to gush, praising wildly

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A US leader rants about beer and loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' is slang for crazy, signalling the anagram; 'about' wraps the word for rave around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Both George Bush senior and junior served as President of the United States.

clue.text: Band with time to focus on beat

parts.note: to focus on something is to watch it
to strap someone is to beat them with a strap

explanation.surface: A band rehearses, keeping time and concentrating on the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band with time' sounds musical but describes a strap that carries a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the band of leather or metal that fastens a timepiece to the wrist.

clue.text: Exultant cry on entering English country area?

indicators.note: the short word for on goes into the country's letters

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom
're' means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone whoops with delight on crossing into an English region.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes' famous shout of discovery is the classic exclamation of triumph.

clue.text: Fragrant plant from Asia to fade when cooked

indicators.note: cooked means altered or falsified, as accounts are cooked, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling Asian plant loses its scent once it hits the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges ASIA TO FADE. 'Fragrant' is ironic: the plant's resin smells pungently sulphurous, hence its nickname devil's dung.
explanation.definitionFit: Asafoetida is a fennel-like plant whose dried resin is used as a strong-smelling spice in Indian cooking.

clue.text: Instructions irritate wealthy husband given boot

parts.note: to rub is to chafe or irritate

indicators.note: given the boot means thrown out, so the husband's letter is removed

parts.note: wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: Instructions that annoy a rich man whose wife has just kicked him out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a set of directions, originally printed in red, as on an exam paper.

clue.text: Ground-breaking if dropped from cup-tie

indicators.note: these two letters are dropped out of the match's word

parts.note: a semi-final is a knockout match in a cup competition
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football commentator wonders whether a pioneering side will be knocked out of the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground-breaking' tempts a football reading, but it is the definition; 'dropped' removes the two letters from the middle of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminal work is highly original and influential, laying ground for what follows.

clue.text: Hamlet's resolution?

definitions.meaning: a hamlet is a small village, a place where people have settled
a resolution of a dispute is an agreed outcome or deal

explanation.walkthrough: The clue invites thoughts of Shakespeare's indecisive prince, but 'Hamlet' is a small village.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small community and an agreement that resolves a dispute.

clue.text: Dull state one gets into being manipulated by others?

indicators.note: the state and the number go inside the word for dull

parts.note: a matte finish is dull, not glossy
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
taken as written: the word one

explanation.surface: Someone falls into a gloomy mood while being pushed around by others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a noun here, a creature, not part of a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet worked by strings is a figure whose movements are controlled entirely by someone else.

clue.text: Something worthless Frenchman found in Spanish city

indicators.note: the Frenchman's letter is found in the city's name

parts.note: León is a city in northern Spain
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A useless Frenchman is tracked down in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a dud, such as a faulty car, is called by this fruit's name.

clue.text: Bring down news boss backing the media

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the editor's abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: An editor supports the media while trying to topple someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but reverses ED to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress something is to push or lower it, as when pressing a key down.

clue.text: Duke superior to soldiers took a shot perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down clue the duke's letter sits above, before, the word for soldiers

parts.note: the ranks are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A duke outranking the troops fires his gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests gunfire but means a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a small measure of spirits, so downing one is an example of having a drink.

clue.text: Long time before November

indicators.note: the period comes before the letter for November

parts.note: a year is a period of time
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time leading up to November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb here, to crave, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to desire it intensely, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Wrong men entered in race

indicators.note: the soldiers' letters are entered in the race's letters

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
OR (other ranks) means ordinary soldiers, men

explanation.surface: A mistake was made when the men were signed up for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' as OR, other ranks, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: In law this is a civil wrong that causes harm and gives grounds for damages.

clue.text: Sound happy for each individual to be heard

indicators.note: the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Each person's contented voice is supposed to be audible.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat makes this low vibrating noise when content, a sound of happiness.

clue.text: Cut some ice bringing peacekeepers into bed

indicators.note: the peacekeepers' letters go into the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

explanation.surface: Someone makes an impression by bringing UN troops into a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut some ice' is an idiom, not skating.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut some ice means to matter or carry weight, and that is what something that matters does.

clue.text: Character or bore on the Tube?

definitions.meaning: a person's quality or standing, as in a man of his worth
the internal diameter of a gun barrel, which is a tube

explanation.surface: Is that a real character, or just a tedious commuter on the London Underground?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground and 'bore' a tedious person; here the tube is a gun barrel and the bore its width.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both quality of character and the internal diameter of a barrel.

clue.text: Strength as may be required in steel construction?

definitions.note: the adjective is the kind of strength needed: strength under tension

indicators.note: construction is the building up of something, so these letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: Engineers ask what strength steel must have for a building job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' rearranges IN STEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tensile strength is resistance to being pulled apart, a key property needed in building steel.

clue.text: Asian person brought about to a loch by Scotsman

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for loch or lake
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A traveller from Asia is taken to a Scottish lake by a local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' reverses TO A L to give LAOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Laos in Southeast Asia is called by this word.

clue.text: Sauce boat lifted

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
lifted means raised, up

explanation.surface: A gravy boat is raised from the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' looks like one dish, but 'Sauce' is the definition and 'boat' a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: This tomato condiment is a common sauce.

clue.text: Busy with habitual response to religious language

parts.note: 'busy' is British slang for a police officer, a cop
a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

explanation.surface: A busy person's knee-jerk reply to religious talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is British slang for a police officer, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: This descendant of ancient Egyptian survives as the liturgical tongue of the Egyptian Christian church.

clue.text: Sleeping around is out

definitions.meaning: unfaithful to a partner, having affairs
wrong or inaccurate, as in a calculation that is out

explanation.surface: Infidelity has gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unfaithful to a partner and false or inaccurate.

clue.text: Cereal much esteemed, and light, leading couples used

indicators.note: the leading two letters of each word, a couple from each, are used

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal is praised for being light, and favoured by pairs of diners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading couples' takes the first two letters of MUCH, ESTEEMED and LIGHT: MU, ES, LI.
explanation.definitionFit: This Swiss mixture of oats, nuts and dried fruit is a breakfast cereal.

clue.text: Minor difference with hot and cold switched round?

indicators.note: switched round means turned the other way, so the plumbing word is read backwards

parts.note: a basin has hot and cold taps

explanation.surface: Someone notices a small change in the bath after the hot and cold are swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difference' is a disagreement here, not a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, a small difference of opinion.

clue.text: Brat's piety looks phony in sacred area

indicators.note: something that looks phony is false or faked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's show of devotion seems fake in a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks phony' rearranges BRATS and PIETY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the part of a church, or a separate building, where baptisms take place.

clue.text: Subordinate gives name and number

parts.note: ether numbs, an anaesthetic is a 'number' (numb-er)

explanation.surface: A junior employee hands over a name and a phone number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as numb-er, something that numbs: ether, an old anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or under, so lower in position, which is what subordinate means.

clue.text: Difficult to shift as certain troops were on Somme?

definitions.meaning: firmly established and hard to move or change

definitions.text: as certain troops were on Somme?
definitions.meaning: dug in to trenches, as soldiers were at the Somme in the First World War

explanation.walkthrough: The Somme was a First World War battle fought from trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both firmly fixed and literally placed in trenches.
